findings: Solved 2026-10-29 on the owner's request (Practice > Book exercises, BOOK-EXERCISES-01): the exercise of PDF 276-279 (printed 273-276) with every printed question in the book's words and order: 19 MCQs, 15 short answer, 6 constructed response (12.5 with parts i-iii), 8 comprehensive questions and 5 numerical problems, solved in English and Roman Urdu.
The book prints no MCQ key; keys worked out from the chapter: 1c 2d 3d 4a 5c 6a 7b 8c 9c 10d 11a 12d 13b 14c 15d 16c 17d 18c 19b.

Doubtful MCQs: 12.4 keyed (a) gluons as in the chapter (12.7, 12.11); in the older Yukawa picture the nucleon-nucleon force is carried by mesons (c). 12.9 keyed (c) hadrons; mesons (d) are a subset. 12.18 keyed (c) uud; (b) udu has the same quarks in another order. 12.13 prints 'atomic member' for atomic number.

Book corrections: Numerical 12.5 prints the electron's rest mass as 0.0000555 u, which gives 0.0517 MeV; the chapter's 0.00055 u gives the printed answer 0.51 MeV. Numerical 12.4 calls the nucleon number N (Eq. 12.1: N is the neutron number; nucleon number is A). CRQ 12.6 prints 'a-particles' for α-particles.
Numerical answers 12.1 (A = 234, Z = 90, thorium), 12.2 (A = 218, Z = 85) and 12.3 (¹₁H proton) agree; 12.4 is a show-that.
Short 12.4(a) prints the emitted particle as e with a faint superscript; read as e⁻ (β⁻ decay with ν̄).

Beyond the chapter: MCQ 12.15 (Abdus Salam and the electroweak theory); Short 12.2 and 12.4 and Numerical 12.2 (naming Rb, Sc, At from Z); Short 12.6 (Fermi-Dirac statistics); CRQ 12.3 (α binding energy about 28 MeV); CRQ 12.4 (α energies 4-9 MeV); CRQ 12.5 (E = hf, p = E/c, h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J s); CRQ 12.6 (Rutherford scattering); Comprehensive 12.3 point 4 (early-universe annihilation); Comprehensive 12.4 (PET scan).
